summary.text: 住 is analyzed as a phono-semantic character: 亻 contributes the person category, and 主 supplies a sound cue. The character commonly means “reside” or “stay”; references also describe “stop” or “remain” as an early or basic use.

formation.text: The supported reference analysis is phono-semantic (形聲): 人 appears in its side form 亻 and contributes the person category, while 主 is the phonetic component. This is a dictionary analysis, not a dated account of the graph’s creation. One imported note labels the character ideographic without explaining that analysis; the more specific 人-plus-主 account is supported by several reference works. 主’s exact original referent is unsettled here, but identifying it is not necessary to its proposed sound role.

components.text: 人 is written as 亻 in 住. It contributes the person category in the phono-semantic analysis; 亻 is the positional side form of 人, not a later replacement.
主 is analyzed as the sound component in 住. Its original depicted referent is not established in this dossier; the selected seal-script-style image is a modern redraw of 主, not an early form of 住.

sound.text: In Baxter–Sagart 2014, 主 and 住 have similar but distinct Old Chinese reconstructions, making a phonetic relationship plausible without establishing its specific sound history.
In Baxter–Sagart 2014, the Middle Chinese forms differ; this comparison is part of the same source-specific reconstruction system.
The supplied local Mandarin readings are zhǔ for 主 and zhù for 住. They are a present-day comparison, not evidence by themselves for an ancient phonetic role.
sound.system: Modern Mandarin, supplied local Unihan readings

history.text: The dossier supports no dated early glyph sequence or graphic change account for 住. A reference says it is absent from Shuowen, while historical-form images mentioned elsewhere were unavailable; this does not establish that the character was absent from earlier scripts. No graphic corruption is demonstrated. The curated image depicts 主 in a modern redraw of a Shuowen seal-script style, not an artifact or an early form of 住.

Old Chinese sound comparisons differ by reconstruction source: Wiktionary reports *tos/*dos for 住 and *tjoʔ for 主, while Baxter–Sagart gives *dro(ʔ)-s and *toʔ respectively. These accounts should remain separate; the Baxter–Sagart comparison makes a sound relationship plausible but does not prove the graph’s formation date or phonetic history.

uncertainties.text: The formation analysis is a supported reference-work account, but the dossier does not date the graph’s formation or provide a verified early glyph sequence for 住. Its absence from Shuowen, as reported here, does not establish absence from earlier scripts.

A usage study reports transmitted Western Han and early medical-text examples for “remain/stop,” and later evidence for “reside,” but manuscript dating and transmission do not establish a securely dated earliest attestation. The reported semantic path is a history of usage, not graphic evolution.

主’s original depicted referent is unsettled in the dossier. Its proposed role as a sound component in 住 does not depend on identifying that referent; the cited Old Chinese comparison supports plausibility rather than proof of the historical sound relation.

Other listed senses and relations include verbal-complement uses, “straight,” use with 駐, and a variant relation with 往. The evidence supplied does not establish their chronology or connection, and does not support treating 住 as a whole-character loan from 主.

senses.period: Western Han and later uses reported; secure earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: A usage account identifies a transmitted Western Han example for “stay/remain” and discusses early medical-text examples, while warning that transmission and dating do not settle the earliest attestation. Reference works also describe “stop/remain” as a basic or early sense.

senses.period: Late Han–Three Kingdoms texts reported; attested more widely later
senses.text: A usage study reports residence uses in late Han–Three Kingdoms texts and says they become dominant by the Eastern Jin. These are reported literary-text attestations rather than securely dated manuscript evidence.
Dictionaries record lodging and staying among the character’s uses, but the supplied evidence does not independently date this sense or establish its precise relation to “stop/remain” and “reside.”

developments.text: A usage account proposes development from stopping or remaining toward lodging and residence. The reported sequence concerns word use; manuscript dating does not establish its exact chronology.

limitations.text: The proposed early examples are transmitted textual evidence, not securely dated manuscript attestations; the earliest use of each sense remains unresolved.
Dictionary lists also include other uses, but a list of glosses without dated evidence does not establish their order or semantic connections.

overview.text: 住 is analyzed with 亻 for the person category and 主 as a sound cue. It commonly means “reside” or “stay”; “stop/remain” is described as an early or basic use.

components.text: 亻 is the side form of 人, contributing the person category in this character.
主 supplies a sound cue. The similar Old Chinese forms make that relationship plausible, though they do not prove its precise history.

relationships.text: In the reference analysis of 住, 亻 is the positional form of 人 and contributes the person category.

Reference works analyze 主 as the sound component. In Baxter–Sagart 2014, 主 *toʔ and 住 *dro(ʔ)-s are similar but distinct Old Chinese reconstructions; this supports plausibility without proving the specific phonetic history.
